Third-Gen Fiat Panda Refuses to Die: Here's a New Pandina Tributo Autobianchi Special Edition
12 photos
Photo: Fiat
Believe it or not, the third generation of the Fiat Panda nameplate has been around since 2011, and a decade and a half later it is not showing any signs of slowing down. Quite the contrary.
The Fiat Panda city car was born in 1980 as a simple, two-box three-door hatchback that was penned by Giorgetto Giugiaro and Aldo Mantovani of Italdesign. The success was legendary, and the original was produced until 2003, for no less than 23 years. The second generation was completely redesigned to bode well for the early 2000s and it lived for less than a decade as the third iteration appeared in 2011 at the Frankfurt Motor Show.
Now, 15 years and many iterations later, the third-generation Fiat Panda has no plans to retire, and the Italian automaker even introduces a new special edition, the fresh Pandina Tributo Autobianchi , set as the new flagship version that also pays homage to “one of the most distinctive names in Italian automotive history.”
The date of its reveal, October 21, 2026, also has a symbolic importance: it connects the past and present because precisely 30 years ago the final Autobianchi Y10 was registered. As a reminder, the Autobianchi Y10, introduced in 1985, was derived from the Fiat Panda platform and reinterpreted “the concept of the compact car through sophisticated styling and refined finishes.”
Now, the new Pandina Tributo Autobianchi, with Pandina being in itself a special version of the Fiat Panda Cross model that pays tribute to the Italian nickname of the car, will stand out with its exclusive perks: an exclusive hue, contrasting black exterior details, dedicated alloy wheels, and various Tributo Autobianchi personalization elements, plus new interior finishes.
More precisely, Fiat’s new Pandina Tributo Autobianchi joins the Pandina range above the Pop, Icon, and Cross trim levels, all available with a hybrid powertrain, wearing a new Platino colour, developed specifically for this version and exclusively available on this special edition. There’s also a contrasting black roof and tailgate, exclusive 15-inch diamond-cut alloy wheels, and more.
Inside, the car has light-sand microfiber seats with a “quadrettoni” pattern and a dedicated logo on the front headrests, plus matching light-sand soft-touch door panel inserts. There’s also a Platino-painted dashboard fascia, dedicated “Tributo Autobianchi” welcome graphics on the instrument cluster and radio, plus bespoke floor mats and other finishes.
The new version will be produced at the Italian plant in Pomigliano d’Arco, and “Pandina Tributo Autobianchi retains all the qualities that have made the model so successful: simplicity, practicality, accessibility and versatility, enriched with a touch of Italian elegance.” Fiat leads the European A segment with the Pandina model, announcing over 100k registrations (86k in Italy) during nine months, up 7% compared to last year.
